title: Julnar of the Sea and King Badr Basim
summary: King Shahriman of Persia had wed Julnar the Sea-Born, an oceanic princess of supernatural beauty who possessed the ancient power to walk beneath the waves and breathe underwater...
keywords: julnar the sea-born and her son king badr basim
full_text:
King Shahriman of Persia had wed Julnar the Sea-Born, an oceanic princess of supernatural beauty who possessed the ancient power to walk beneath the waves and breathe underwater like a creature of the air. Their son, Prince Badr Basim—whose name meant 'Full Moon that Smiles'—inherited the noble qualities of both the land and the sea.

When Badr attained manhood, he heard of Princess Jauharah, daughter of King Al-Samandal, sovereign of the underwater coral empires, celebrated as the peerless jewel of the ocean.

Seeking her hand with pure intentions, Badr traveled to the undersea kingdoms with his mother's blessing. However, King Al-Samandal was proud and wrathful, refusing to let an earthly prince wed his oceanic daughter, and in his fury, sought to imprison Badr.

Badr escaped, washed ashore on an enchanted island ruled by Queen Lab, an evil sorceress who transformed handsome travelers into beasts. Recognizing the enchantment with his sharp intellect, Badr outwitted the sorceress, broke her spells, and restored forty captive princes to their human forms!

Princess Jauharah, hearing of Badr’s heroic valor, wisdom, and chivalric defense of the oppressed, fell in love with his noble character.

She reconciled her father with the land kingdom of Persia, and their magnificent royal wedding was celebrated both on the marble terraces of Shiraz and in the glowing coral palaces of the sea, uniting the realms of earth and ocean in perpetual peace.
moral: Noble character, filial respect, and courageous endurance bridge the worlds of the earth and the ocean.
